subject: Quantium reserved throughput degradation — urgent exec visibility requested
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, ops@quantium.com, Mark Davison <mark.davison@quantium.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quantium: reserved throughput drop and 5xx spike — initial heads-up

Team —

I'm escalating a high-severity signal from Quantium (QNT-2026-042). Over the past ~90 minutes their reserved-capacity endpoint backed by dedicated GPU pool D-Pool-11 has seen:
- Sustained GPU utilization at ~98–100% across the pool.
- 99th percentile latency for generation calls jumped from ~220ms to ~890ms.
- Error rate (5xx) increased from baseline ~0.2% to ~3.8%.
- Observed throughput is ~40% below the committed reserved qps for their tier.

I've attached a snapshot (quantium_metrics_oct08.pdf) with dashboard charts. Customer ops (ops@quantium.com) also cc'd — Mark (CTO) asked for executive visibility and an ETA on mitigation.

Requested immediate asks:
1) Quick triage (Aditya) — confirm whether this is noisy-neighbor vs model-level regression.
2) Ops mitigations (Marissa/Evelyn) — options for temporary traffic re-routing, burst approval, or routing to compatible model variants.
3) Exec coordination (Rishi/Jonas) — if we need emergency burst credits or a billing/credit conversation, we should brief leadership and prepare a short one-pager for Quantium's CTO.

This is impacting production traffic for their top-of-funnel inference. Please reply with status updates in-thread; if we need a war room, I'll create and invite.

-Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: quantium_metrics_oct08.pdf
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, ops@quantium.com, Mark Davison <mark.davison@quantium.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantium: reserved throughput drop and 5xx spike — initial heads-up

Jonas — quick triage from the serving/runtime side. Raw observations:
- Pool D-Pool-11 shows a concentration of long-lived KV cache entries from a single slot (QNT-tokenset-74) that are not benefiting from prefix caching; it looks like a sudden burst of long-context reranks (lengths >512) that prevents efficient batching.
- Kernel metrics: small-batch overhead dominates; effective batching has collapsed to ~1.8 avg inference per GPU instance.
- Memory pressure triggered more frequent KV eviction which is causing repeated cold-starts and duplicated work.

Short-term mitigations we can push in the next 15–30 minutes (requires coordination):
A) Route 15% of their traffic to a hosted general-purpose endpoint (model variant: rwd-7b-pp-8bit) that is compatible with their calls — reduces load on dedicated pool but slightly increases per-token latency.
B) Apply an emergency throttling policy (token caps + concurrency window) for their heaviest routes to preserve tail latency for the rest of traffic.
C) Spin up a temporary burst on adjacent dedicated cluster (burst request: BRST-quantium-10) — this requires exec approval for emergency capacity and will incur short-term commitment.
D) Short-term model change: enable a 4-bit quantized variant of the same policy for non-critical routes (we can flip a feature flag).

I'll prepare an excerpt showing predicted tail-latency improvement for each option. If we approve routing + throttling now, we should see the 99p latency drop within ~10–15 minutes.

-Aditya
Principal Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Quantium: reserved throughput drop and 5xx spike — customer context + contractual notes

Forwarding customer context and Ops notes.

Quantium has a reserved capacity contract with an SLA clause for throughput and tail latency. They have an upcoming product launch next week, which increases the criticality. From CS: customer is seeing revenue impact on specific routes (nlp.rerank/long-context) and is already rotating on-call into incident rooms.

From: Sarah L. <ops@quantium.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 09:35:12 -0700
Subject: Full production impact — we need a temporary fix now

Hi Redwoods —
We started seeing request timeouts at 08:45 local. Traffic surges coincided with a marketing send; endpoints are critical to our checkout QA flows. Please advise gamma plan.

Attachments: quantium_incident_timeline.xlsx

Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantium: reserved throughput drop and 5xx spike — executive actions

Thanks for the signal and the proposed mitigations. Directive:
1) Approve emergency burst BRST-quantium-10 for 2 hours now. Finance: please treat as billable emergency capacity; we will reconcile with customer credits later. Marissa — coordinate payment authorization with Finance.
2) Implement Aditya's routing + throttling combination immediately: route 15% to hosted variant + apply concurrency caps on rerank routes. Prioritize tail-latency improvement.
3) Legal/Contracts: pre-approve language for a temporary SLA adjustment and a one-time credit (up to 10% of last month's invoice) should we miss committed throughput during this window. Marissa, please get the short legal blurb ready and notify customer.
4) Prepare a one-page exec summary for Quantium's CTO and our CEO — include timeline, actions, ETA to recovery, and next steps (procurement for additional reserved slots). Jonas — you own the one-pager; Marissa/Evelyn help with customer impact language.
5) 30-minute sync with Quantium CTO in 30 minutes. Jonas, set up the meeting and include Aditya for technical Q&A.

I will be on the call. Keep all updates in-thread.

-Rishi
SVP, Customer Success & Partnerships
From: Mark Davison <mark.davison@quantium.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quantium: reserved throughput drop and 5xx spike — urgent

Jonas/Rishi —
Thanks for the quick responses and the proposed mitigations. We are OK with routing up to 20% of non-critical traffic to an alternate endpoint if that prevents checkout failures. Please provide expected recovery ETA for the 99p latency and the 5xx rate after the routing + throttling are applied.

Attached is a short incident timeline from our side (quantium_incident_timeline.xlsx). We're prioritizing protection of checkout flows — we will accept a temporary small uptick in tail latency on non-critical analytics routes.

-Mark Davison

Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantium: reserved throughput drop and 5xx spike — actions in place and meeting invite

Mark —
Thanks. Actions we have applied (now live):
- Route 15% of non-critical traffic to hosted endpoint rwd-7b-pp-8bit (started 11:55 PDT).
- Concurrency caps and token windows applied to /nlp.rerank routes (11:58 PDT).
- Emergency burst BRST-quantium-10 authorized and started at 12:00 PDT (2-hour window).
- Legal has a draft note for a one-time credit; Marissa will send to your billing contact after sync.

Expected impact: we predict 99p latency to fall from ~890ms to <300ms within ~12–18 minutes after throttling takes effect; 5xx rate should drop below 1% in that window. We will monitor and post updated charts in the shared drive link.

Meeting: invites sent for 12:35–13:05 PDT (30 minutes) — join if you can; agenda: timeline, mitigations, next steps (procure additional reserved slots / capacity plan).

Attached: exec_one_pager_quantium.md (short summary for CTO and our leadership).

-Jonas
